result.topic_en: Fragments on making pairs of quadratic forms simultaneously squares: forms for m,n making aa+mmbb and aa+nnbb squares, conditions on N so that xx+Ayy and xx+Nyy are both squares, a Diophantine problem with two quadratic conditions in x, and the start of solving two simultaneous quadratic equalities.
result.transcription:
Fragmenta ex Adversariis depromta. 253

Ut formulae $aa+mmbb$ et $aa+nnbb$ reddi possint quadrata, numeros $m$ et $n$ ex talibus formis sumi oportet, (ubi quidem ratio inter $m$ et $n$ est definienda)
$pq(rr-1)$, $pr(qq-1)$, $qr(pp-1)$, $p(qq-rr)$, $q(pp-rr)$, $r(pp-qq)$
$p(qqrr-1)$, $q(pprr-1)$, $r(ppqq-1)$, $ppqq-rr$, $pprr-qq$, $qqrr-pp$,
$ppqqrr-1$,
quae formulae omnes ita sunt comparatae, ut si earum quadratis addatur idem quadratum $4ppqqrr$, proveniant quadrata.
A. m. T. I. p. 122.

Problema. Dato numero $A$, invenire conditiones numeri $N$, ut ambae istae formulae $xx+Ayy$, $xx+Nyy$ simul fieri possint quadrata.

Solutio. Ponatur $A=\mu\nu$, pro casu scilicet, quo habet factores, et priori formae satisfiet sumendo $x=\mu pp-\nu qq$ et $y=2pq$, tum enim erit $xx+Ayy=(\mu pp+\nu qq)^2$. Simul vero etiam altera formula evadet quadratum, si fuerit $N=mmppqq+m(\mu pp-\nu qq)$; tum enim erit
$xx+Nyy=(\mu pp-\nu qq)^2+4mppqq(\mu pp-\nu qq)+4mmp^4q^4=(\mu pp-\nu qq+2mppqq)^2$,
erit ergo $N=mmppqq+m(\mu pp-\nu qq)$, ubi $m$ pro lubitu assumere licet. Quin etiam pro $m$ fractiones assumere licet, ita ut pro $N$ nihilominus prodeant numeri integri, sumto enim $m=n+\frac{\nu}{pp}$, tum enim fiet
$N=(n+\frac{\nu}{pp})(nppqq+\mu pp)=(npp+\nu)(nqq+\mu)$.
A. m. T. I. p. 128.

72.
(N. Fuss I.)

Problema Diophanteum. Invenire numerum $x$ ut his duabus conditionibus satisfiat
$xx+2ax+mmc=\Box$ et $xx+2bx+nnc=\Box$,
cujus solutio particularis est
$x=\frac{(nna-mmb)^2-mmnn(m-n)^2c}{2mn(m-n)(na-mb)}$.
Ita si proponantur hae duae formulae: $xx+2ax+c=\Box$ et $xx+2bx+c=\Box$, sumatur $m=1$ et $n=-1$
eritque $x=\frac{(a-b)^2-4c}{4(a+b)}$.
A. m. T. II. p. 154.

73.

Problema. Resolvere has duas aequalitates:
$(2+2a)xx+(2-2a)yy=4AA$ et $(2+2b)xx+(2-2b)yy=4BB$.

Solutio. Hinc ergo primo erit $4A^2+4B^2=(4+2(a+b))xx+(4-2(a+b))yy$; posito ergo
$a+b=2c$, erit $A^2+B^2=(1+c)xx+(1-c)yy$.
Deinde vero erit $4A^2-4B^2=2(a-b)(xx-yy)$, unde posito $a-b=2d$, erit $A^2-B^2=d(xx-yy)$. Statuatur ergo $A+B=x+y$ eritque $A-B=d(x-y)$. Addantur quadrata eritque
$2A^2+2B^2=(x+y)^2+dd(x-y)^2=2(1+c)xx+2(1-c)yy$,
quae evoluta fit $(1+dd)xx+(1-dd)2xy+(1+dd)yy=2(1+c)xx+2(1-c)yy$, sive
$(dd-2c-1)xx+2(1-dd)xy+(dd+2c-1)yy=0$,
sive $(dd-1)(xx-2xy+yy)-2c(xx-yy)=0$,
